pixel_metrics_withdrawn.why: The copy-mode scene renders the attach client's status bar, which carries a live uptime clock, and a copy-mode cursor whose row depends on when the capture lands. At 200x60 an A/A run of ONE binary against itself reproduced the same 413-pixel delta as the A/B, on the same three text rows (cursor cell on rows 1 and 2, clock on row 59). The 80x24 and 120x40 arms read 0/0 today by luck, not by construction, so committing them as exact-0 metrics was a latent flake. Copy-mode evidence is kept as deterministic TEXT instead: the oldest retained line is identical on both binaries at all three breakpoints.

binary_identity.question: Does the test-module change reach the shipped binary?
binary_identity.answer: No — proven by controlled experiment rather than argued from cfg(test) semantics.
binary_identity.naive_comparison: make release at c64efb1 vs 32f192a produced DIFFERENT binaries, 33514664 vs 33514656 bytes.
binary_identity.cause: crates/shux/build.rs and crates/shux-rpc/build.rs shell out to `git rev-parse --short HEAD` and embed it as SHUX_GIT_SHA; the binaries self-report "shux 0.48.0 (c64efb1)" and "shux 0.48.0 (32f192a)". The 8-byte delta is that embedded string, not the diff.
binary_identity.controlled_experiment: With HEAD left at 32f192a so SHUX_GIT_SHA is held constant, built make release twice, changing only the content of grid.rs (32f192a content, then `git checkout c64efb1 -- crates/shux-vt/src/grid.rs`).
binary_identity.consequence: The pixel, daemon-artifact and corpus measurements taken at c64efb1 describe the identical executable and transfer by identity, not by argument. They were deliberately NOT re-run for 32f192a.

pixel_metrics_provenance: All 18 committed metrics were measured at c64efb1. They are carried forward unchanged for 32f192a on the strength of binary_identity above, which shows the release executable is byte-identical once the embedded git SHA is held constant. This is a deliberate, stated decision, not an omission.

regression_proof_32f192a.method: Removed only line 653 (`self.evicted = 0`) from reset_blank at 32f192a. The target test was left byte-identical: sha256 of the extracted fn body is 6c5928c22abe8a6a on both the fixed and unfixed trees.
regression_proof_32f192a.failure_message: reset: a grid the recycling branch would reuse untouched is still counting from a discarded grid's base — left: 9, right: 0, at grid.rs:2163
regression_proof_32f192a.right_reason: The failure lands on the per-candidate loop assertion, NOT on the new non-vacuity guard. On the unfixed tree the reset candidate is still admitted (admitted=true, evicted=9), so the guard passes on both trees and it is the property assertion that bites. The message names the offending candidate.
candidate_census_fixed_tree: fresh:        admitted=true  evicted=0 mutations=0 rows=4 rawlen=4 reject_on=[]
scrolled:     admitted=false evicted=9 mutations=9 rows=4 rawlen=4 reject_on=[tally]
reset:        admitted=true  evicted=0 mutations=0 rows=4 rawlen=4 reject_on=[]
resized:      admitted=true  evicted=0 mutations=0 rows=4 rawlen=4 reject_on=[]
restructured: admitted=false evicted=2 mutations=4 rows=2 rawlen=2 reject_on=[tally,rows,rawlen]
regression_proof_32f192a.reset_admitted_for_the_right_reason: Yes. reset is scrolled.clone() + reset_blank; its parent has identical geometry but mutations=9 and is rejected. Admission therefore turns on reset_blank zeroing the write tally — the actual recycling path — not on geometry.

findings_this_run.F6_restructured_candidate_is_triple_reje: P3 observation, not a defect. The new `restructured` candidate is rejected on tally, rows AND rawlen (2 rows vs the 4 requested), so it can never reach the admitted set and contributes nothing to the property being asserted over candidates. Its value is the assert!(restructured.evicted() > 0) line, which pins the F1 counterexample as executable documentation. Worth a word in the comment so a reader does not assume it exercises the admitted path. By construction no candidate with a moved base can ever be admitted except via reset_blank, which is exactly why reset is the discriminator.
